name: Exodus
tagline: Non-custodial multi-chain crypto wallet for desktop, mobile and browser, with in-app swaps and staking.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. The wallet itself is free to download; revenue comes from spreads and fees on in-app swaps and similar services.

verdictSummary: An agent can absolutely generate something that calls itself a crypto wallet in an afternoon, and that is exactly the problem. The hard part is not the UI, it is key generation, seed handling, encrypted storage, transaction construction and signing across dozens of unrelated chains, plus fee estimation that does not silently burn your money. Exodus also carries node and indexer infrastructure, swap provider integrations, hardware wallet support, and years of adversarial review by people who steal crypto for a living. A homemade wallet is a single bug away from an irreversible, uninsured, unrecoverable loss. Build a watch-only tracker instead and keep your keys somewhere that has been audited.
coreLoopDIY: A local watch-only portfolio tracker: paste in public addresses, pull balances from public RPC and explorer APIs, price them, and show holdings and history without ever touching a private key.
requirements: Free API keys for a price feed and one or two chain explorers, in .env
Public wallet addresses you want to watch
Node 20 and a willingness to accept rate limits on free API tiers
whatYouLose: Actual custody: you cannot send, swap, stake or sign anything, by design
Native desktop and mobile apps with synced state across devices
Hardware wallet pairing and the seed phrase recovery flow
Built-in swap and staking providers, and the fee estimation that makes them not-terrible
Broad asset coverage: you get the handful of chains you wire up, not thousands of tokens
Security auditing, and someone to blame other than yourself
moatNotes: Wallets are a trust product first and a software product second. Nobody moves five figures into an app they generated last Tuesday.
whyPeopleStillPay: People do not pay Exodus a subscription, they pay it a spread, and they do it because the alternative is holding the sharp end of cryptography themselves. The value is that key handling, signing and multi-chain node access have been done many millions of times without the app losing anyone's funds, and that reputation cannot be one-shotted. Add hardware wallet support, mobile parity and swap routing on top and the gap widens further. The one thing you genuinely can self-build is the boring part: seeing what you own without handing an address book to a third party.
notes: A watch-only tracker is a one-sitting build; a wallet you would trust with real money is not. The moat is custody trust: audited key handling, signing across dozens of chains, and years of not being drained.
prompt:
Build a local-first, watch-only crypto portfolio tracker. It must never handle private keys or seed phrases.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Node 20, TypeScript, Express for the API
- Vite + React + TypeScript for the UI, plain CSS, no component library
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, single file db at ./data/portfolio.db
- Run both with a single `npm run dev` using concurrently

Features in scope:
- Add, label and remove watch addresses. Each row: chain, address, label.
- Support exactly three chains: Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana. Read balances from public endpoints configured in .env (an Ethereum RPC URL, a Solana RPC URL, a Bitcoin explorer base URL).
- For Ethereum, also fetch balances for a user-supplied list of ERC-20 token contract addresses per wallet.
- Fetch USD prices from a price API with the key in .env. Cache prices in SQLite for 10 minutes.
- Dashboard: total portfolio value, a table of holdings grouped by asset, and a per-address breakdown.
- Daily value snapshot written to SQLite on refresh, plus a simple line chart of total value over time drawn with SVG, no chart library.
- Manual "Refresh" button and an optional background refresh every 15 minutes.
- CSV export of current holdings.

Explicitly out of scope, do not implement:
- Key generation, seed phrases, signing, sending, swapping, staking
- User accounts, auth, telemetry, analytics, any cloud service
- Any chain beyond the three listed

Requirements:
- All secrets and endpoints in .env, with a committed .env.example. Never log them.
- Handle API failures and rate limits gracefully: show stale cached values with a "last updated" timestamp rather than crashing.
- README with setup steps and a blunt warning that this is read-only and is not a wallet.
